Science made easy.

debug(research) → knowledge

Ten batches. A token system, a component library with its states, a navigation shell at three widths, and 162 product screens from cold start to institutional audit. Every one of the 411 backlog features now carries a status, checkable row by row on the coverage index. Two people have to be able to read every screen we build — Alex Rivera, who needs credible context before repeating a failure, and Dr Camille Laurent, who needs the lab's knowledge to survive the people who made it.

EVALUATION LAYER

IS THE PROTOTYPE ANY GOOD?

6 boards · nothing new designed · this is what makes it checkable
K1Coverage audit
77.6%designed-equivalent · not 91%
Status counts, a completion bar per domain A–T, and a gap list of 13 features with the reason for each. Two are genuine misses we cannot defend.
K2Usability evaluation
Seven flows, each with the task as the user states it, clicks from entry to completion, the decision points where the wrong path is plausible, and a drop-off rating per step. Five high-risk steps.
K3Heuristic review
2 catastrophic10 major19 minor
Ten screens against Nielsen's ten. The two catastrophic findings are both irreversible-action failures: the licence picker and the append-only notebook.
K4Consistency audit
Five rules measured across 53 boards by counting source tokens. Visibility chip, status palette and AI sources pass. The orange budget has 6 breaches. Focus states fail outright — 0 of 53.
K5Open questions
Twelve decisions the brief did not settle and I made anyway — each with what I chose, the case for and against, the cost of reversing, and a recommendation. Four block the build.
K6Walkthrough deck
Fourteen slides for the other five founders: two personas, seven flows, the five differentiating screens, coverage, what we refused, and the four decisions we need. Presents full-screen; exports to PDF.

[ 005 ]

THE SEAMS

every deviation from the brief, and everything invented to fill a gap
D1 · THE BIGGEST ONE — TWO DESIGN SYSTEMS WERE IN PLAY
This project has the Industry design system attached — steel-blue #5980a6, Barlow Condensed over Barlow, 4px radius, blueprint line-drawing objects with + registration marks. The brief specifies a different one: orange #FF4D00, JetBrains Mono over Inter, radius 0–2. They cannot both be the surface. I resolved it by splitting grammar from palette: Industry's structural language is kept — hairline 1px frames, square corners, transparent cards that are line drawings rather than filled surfaces, the modular grid, corner registration marks (visible on this page's cards and on the shell artboards), Lucide icons at stroke 1.5, elevation by border rather than shadow — and its colour and type are replaced wholesale by the brief's tokens. The Industry stylesheet still loads on every board, but its steel accent is never painted. If the founders want the attached system to win on colour too, that is a token swap on one board and a re-export, not a redesign.
D2 · INTER FOR BODY — FLAGGED AS ASKED
Requested by the brief and flagged on the design-system board where the founders will see it. Chrome stays mono; prose at 14px and above is Inter. The cost of rejecting it is roughly 15% reading speed on long answers.
D3 · THE COMPONENT LIBRARY IS TWO BOARDS
One library, split atoms / molecules. A single board holding all 44 specimens with all states was slow to load and slower to edit across the batches ahead. Same tokens, same numbering — A01–A16, M01–M28.
D4 · INVENTED: M28, THE AI RETRIEVAL BLOCK
"AI for retrieval, not authority" is a hard rule with no component to enforce it. So there is one: a retrieval block that cannot render without at least one clickable source artifact and a route to a human. It has no accept button — AI cannot resolve a thread.
D5 · INVENTED: THE ORCID MARKER
The brief asks for an ORCID-verified marker without specifying one. It is a 3px green rule across the foot of the avatar — legible at 20px, survives greyscale, and cannot be confused with a presence dot. Unverified accounts get the same rule in --rule grey, so absence is visible too.
D6 · INVENTED: FOUR REPUTATION AXES
"Reputation axis meter" named no axes. I chose Answers · Reproduction · Null results · Mentorship. Null results is scored, because a platform that treats negative results as first-class has to pay people for them. Change the axes and the component does not change.
D7 · TWO EXTRA COLUMNS ON THE INDEX
The brief listed ID · Domain · Feature · Screens · Status. I added REL and MOSCOW from the spreadsheet, because choosing which batch comes next is unreadable without them. Domain is a group header and a letter badge rather than 411 repeated cells.
D8 · DARK MODE IS NOT AN INVERSION
Straight inversion put --ok, --err, --info and --signal below 4.5:1 on #0D0D0D, so all four were re-valued. Names are stable; hexes are not. Toggle it on the design-system board.
D9 · FOCUS RING FLIPS ON ORANGE
Focus-visible is 2px --signal at 2px offset — except on the orange primary button, where an orange ring on orange is invisible. There it becomes --ink. One exception, applied consistently.
D10 · WHAT "CAPTURE" MEANS ON MOBILE
The brief fixed the five mobile tabs but not their contents. Capture stands in for Methods, Projects, Data, Code and Write: the phone gets an observation, a photo or a failed run into a project in under 30 seconds. Authoring is desktop work.
D11 · TABLET BEHAVIOUR IS INVENTED
834 was given as a breakpoint with no behaviour. At 834 the rail locks to 56px icon-only and the context panel becomes a slide-over; below 1280 the panel collapses by default. Nothing is removed, only re-hosted.
D12 · THE ORANGE BUDGET, SPENT
Three orange elements maximum. On the desktop shell they are: the active rail marker, the Create button, the notification count. Everything else that wants attention uses --flag yellow or a border weight step. Later batches inherit this budget.
D13 · TOGGLES ARE SQUARE
A pill toggle breaks the radius rule, so the switch is a 36×20 rectangle with a square knob and no easing. It reads as an instrument switch, which is the point, but it is less familiar than a pill. Say if that trade is wrong.
D14 · 11px IS A FLOOR, NOT A SIZE
The scale bottoms out at 11px. It is permitted only for uppercase mono labels tracked at 0.08em or more, never for prose. Dense is the brief; unreadable is not.
D15 · SPECIMENS CARRY REAL CONTENT
Every molecule is filled with one running scenario — Alex Rivera's knock-in efficiency collapsing above passage 18 — rather than lorem. It is invented content. It is there because a component that only works with three-word labels is not finished, and because the same scenario can carry straight into the feature batches.
D16 · WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT
No feature screens, as instructed. Also no imagery treatment: Industry duotones photographs, and this system has no photographs at all — the brief bans illustration and the product's images are data, which get the artifact-card frame instead.
